title: Skills routing and ACD
blurb: Dynamic delivery, routing attributes, channel lock, and what safe mode still routes.

lessons.title: Two ways dynamic delivery hands work out
lessons.summary: Dynamic delivery routes on how long an agent has been Available and on proficiency. Automatic delivery paces about every 15 seconds. Agent-request delivery waits for Request Interaction or +1 Contact.
objectives: Say which agent apps require dynamic delivery
Leave AI Routing as an optional extra

p: The dynamic delivery page says interactions route based on how long agents have been Available and on their proficiency in the skill. If AI Routing is enabled, it also considers which agent is most likely to help meet a target metric. Bullseye routing, routing attributes, or both can narrow the pool.
That is a different sentence from the static-delivery priority formula on the other track. This lesson does not copy that formula onto dynamic delivery.

Automatic delivery gives the agent one voice interaction plus as many digital chat, email, or work item interactions as you allow. The pace is about 15 seconds. It does not load-balance. If the agent rejects an interaction, requests continue until the queue is empty or the agent meets the interaction threshold.

Agent-request delivery gives one voice contact plus one chat, email, or work item. Agent Workspace (Agent) uses a Request Interaction button. MAX uses +1 Contact. The next type follows ACD skill priority and acceleration. The agent cannot choose the type. Agent capacity profiles work with both types.

Dynamic delivery is supported in MAX, Salesforce Agent, Agent Workspace (Agent), Agent Workspace (Embedded), Agent Workspace for Microsoft Teams, and Agent Workspace (Browser Extension). It is required for those Agent Workspace applications. It does not support Advanced Chat v1. Advanced Chat v2 is supported in MAX only, and without co-browse.

lessons.title: Turn dynamic delivery on, and do not casually turn it off
lessons.summary: The business unit's Contact Handling Method becomes Dynamic Delivery (Recommended). After that, NiCE recommends asking the account representative before you go back to static delivery.

p: The enable page's required permission is ACD > ACD Configuration > Business Unit Time Zones. Open ACD, go to ACD Configuration > Business Units, click Edit, and set Contact Handling Method to Dynamic Delivery (Recommended). Read the verification pop-up, click Yes, then Done.

Switching changes the agent experience. Train people on the extra cognitive load and on the interface, including manually accepting contacts if you enable that. After the system uses dynamic delivery, NiCE recommends consulting the account representative before reverting to static delivery. Also verify team or user contact-delivery settings for voice. The page says those settings may become disabled in the switch.

cites.title: Enable Dynamic Delivery for Your Organization

p: If integrated matching is not on yet, Digital Experience is on, and active digital channels have long-running interactions, complete the page's preparation first. Interactions already in queue that the job does not process receive a max priority of 1000 when integrated matching is enabled.

The page's example job tags the next 500 matching interactions at the start of each hour and sets their max priority to 50, or to the number you configure. Acceleration and max priority on digital skills work only after integrated matching is enabled. New contacts then take the skill or digital ReqAgent settings.

lessons.title: Routing attributes, five at a time
lessons.summary: Attributes are custom traits inside a skill. Dynamic delivery can use several in one action. Static delivery can use one. More than five on one action can leave the contact with nobody.

p: The routing attributes page calls them a bullseye method. They are custom traits that narrow the pool inside an ACD skill. The examples are languages, state-issued licenses, and product certifications. You assign them on the user profile and use them in Studio.

The actions named are Reqagent, UpdateContact, Queuevm, Queuecallback, and CountAgents. You can assign many attributes to one user and many users to one attribute. The tenant can hold as many as you want. Up to 5,000 can be active at once.

A dynamic-delivery script can reference multiple routing attributes at a time. A static-delivery script can reference one. Multiple attributes have to be enabled by the account representative. Digital interactions can use attributes only after that representative enables dynamic delivery.

The page says to use no more than five attributes on one routing action, or the contact can sit with no matching agent. SLAs stay on the skill. You cannot put an SLA on the attribute. If you use WFM, read that product's guidance first: the IEX Distribution Rules Guide, or the CXone WFM help.

lessons.title: Proficiency for one user, or for one skill
lessons.summary: On dynamic delivery, the ACD user Skills tab changes many skills for one person. Changing many people on one skill is a different screen.
objectives: Not confuse the two bulk edits

p: The proficiency page is specific to dynamic delivery. Static delivery has its own help. The required permission is ACD > Contact Settings > ACD Users Edit.
Open ACD, go to ACD Users, open the profile, open the Skills tab, and change the Proficiency dropdown on each assigned skill. Then click Save Proficiencies.

cites.title: Configure User Skill Proficiency for Dynamic Delivery

p: Changing proficiency through ACD users updates many or all skills for that one user. Changing many or all users on a single skill is done through the skills feature, not this tab.
This lesson does not invent the proficiency numbers. The page tells you where to edit. It does not print a scale.

lessons.title: Channel lock, elevation, and integrated matching
lessons.summary: Channel lock turns AND into OR. Elevation has a table. Integrated matching compares voice, work items, and digital by priority, and it is on by default for new systems.

p: With channel lock off, an agent whose Total Contact Count is 3 can have one voice interaction and two chats at the same time. With channel lock on, that agent can have one voice or two chats, not both. When the locked channel ends, other configured channels can arrive. The agent may never reach the total count, because they are limited to the channel they are locked to.

Any agent can elevate a contact. Chat can go to email, voice, or SMS. Email can go to voice or SMS. Voice can go to email or SMS. Work items and voicemail can go to email, voice, or SMS. SMS can go to email or voice. The empty cells on the page are left empty here.

Integrated matching compares priority across voice (inbound, Personal Connection, and Outbound Engagement (SmartReach)), work items, and digital, and delivers the highest priority first. It uses acceleration and max priority from the ACD skill or the digital REQAGENT action. It is available when dynamic delivery and Digital Experience are on. Both are enabled by default on new systems. An existing system needs the account representative.

Digital chats use the Chats threshold, emails use Emails, SMS uses SMS, and other digital channels use the Digital setting. Those settings are at user and team level. For reporting, only one digital interaction has focus, taken from the cursor and the active part of the agent application. The metrics named are Concurrent Time, Agent Time, Productivity Rate, Elevations, Elevated, and Parent ContactID.

lessons.title: Least occupied, most occupied, and safe mode
lessons.summary: Tenant Management names Least Occupied and Most Occupied under advanced routing. Safe mode still routes, but routing attributes and bullseye ranges do not apply. Safe mode is a North America behavior.
objectives: Not export safe mode outside North America

p: The Manage Tenants page, under ACD advanced routing, describes Multiple Attributes as routing on more than one routing attribute. Least Occupied routes to agents with the fewest active contacts who have not hit their limit, to spread work. Most Occupied routes to agents with the most active contacts who have not hit their limit, to use availability.
Those are feature descriptions on the tenant page. This lesson does not invent the click path that turns them on. The cell on that table says No settings for the ACD application row.

If a major problem is detected, the system enters safe mode with limited functionality. It still routes interactions. It turns on and off by itself. Skill priority and target agent still apply. So do the agent and team contact-handling threshold, Channel Lock, Request Contact, and Auto Focus. Routing attributes and bullseye ranges do not currently apply.

Safe mode is only for systems in North America. If the system is in North America and uses dynamic delivery, safe mode is already on. Opting out is a request to the account representative. The refused-state rules are also different: an Available agent who refuses any contact enters Refused. A Working agent who refuses a digital interaction, or lets it time out, does not. An agent connected to the agent leg cannot refuse a contact.
